Title: July 23, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting
Overview: The council amended its agenda, approved the consent agenda, and continued the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan adoption to August 6, 2026. After a long public hearing on the Boulder Municipal Airport's continued operation, the council voted 8-1 to approve continued indefinite operation with a condition that any FAA grant carrying perpetuity obligations come back to council for a vote before acceptance. Councilmember Wallik resigned from council at the end of the meeting.

Topic1.Title: Roll Call and Agenda Amendment
Topic1.Summary: The council took roll with all members present and a quorum established. The agenda was amended to continue item 3A (BVCP adoption) and add items 2E (special counsel appointment for code of conduct complaints) and 2F (holding the July 30 special meeting in person). The amendment passed unanimously.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic2.Summary: The consent agenda (items 2A through 2F) was approved unanimously. Item 2E authorized the city attorney to appoint special counsel because the city attorney's office had a conflict in investigating a complaint against a board member under the code of conduct. Council also praised the firefighters union for progress on collective bargaining charter language for a future ballot.

Topic3.Title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan Adoption Continued
Topic3.Summary: Staff introduced the BVCP adoption, the first public hearing, and the four bodies reviewing it. Council agreed to open and continue the hearing because of limited time and high public interest. The item was continued to August 6, 2026, and the motion passed unanimously.

Topic4.Title: Airport Public Hearing Presentation
Topic4.Summary: Transportation and Mobility staff presented updated financial scenarios for the Boulder Municipal Airport, including indefinite operation with and without FAA grants. Staff estimated a deficit of about $7 million to $26 million depending on the scenario and identified alternative revenue ideas such as landing fees, hangar development, and solar. Staff said no single alternative would close the gap, and that FAA grants carry perpetual obligations for land acquisition.

Topic5.Title: Council Questions to Staff and Special Counsel
Topic5.Summary: Councilmembers asked about alternative financing, the near-term FAA grant deadlines, and whether the city could restrict noise. Special outside counsel explained federal obligations, FAA perpetuity conditions, and litigation risks and timelines, including Santa Monica's roughly 12-year dispute. Staff also noted the city's position in ongoing litigation that the perpetuity requirement does not apply.

Topic6.Title: Public Hearing on Airport Operations
Topic6.Summary: Speakers were limited to two minutes each and roughly 70 people signed up. Supporters cited emergency medevac and firefighting uses, flight training and youth programs, research flights, economic impact, and the value of unleaded fuel and quieter aircraft. Opponents raised noise and lead concerns, land-use and perpetuity risks, the need for a public vote, and the view that landing fees and self-sustaining models were unexamined. Many speakers asked the council to put the question to voters.

Topic7.Title: Council Deliberation and Motions
Topic7.Summary: Councilmembers discussed fiscal risk, deferred maintenance, long-term land value, climate and wildfire needs, and the value of aviation to the community. A motion by Councilmember Shuhart for a one-year waiting period on perpetuity-covenant obligations was defeated 6 to 3. A staff-recommended motion to approve continued operation was then amended by Councilmember Spear to require council approval of the next FAA grant with perpetuity obligations, and the amendment passed 6 to 3. The amended motion passed 8 to 1.

Topic8.Title: Councilmember Resignation
Topic8.Summary: Councilmember Wallik made a personal privilege statement opposing the airport decision as a surrender of land in perpetuity and announced his immediate resignation from council. Other members expressed regret and thanked him for his service, and staff expressed their respect for his decision.

Topic9.Title: Adjournment
Topic9.Summary: The mayor closed the meeting at 10:25 p.m. after the closing remarks and staff comments concluded.
